title: Experiment: the `server-only` guard on an app-side adapter, with `lib/` left unmarked
summary: `lib/planning.js` carries no marker and stays importable by plain Node — verified by importing it in a bare `node -e` process, which returned the artifact value. An `app/server/planning.js` adapter carries `import 'server-only'` and re-exports from it. A Server Component importing the adapter built and rendered the value. A `'use client'` component importing the adapter FAILED the build at `./app/server/planning.js:1:1`, quoting the import line and the re-export beneath it, with the correct App Router message: the module is a Client Component because one of its parents is marked `use client`.

facts.layout: lib/ as a sibling of app/, plain relative import

omissions.reason: One adapter re-exporting two functions was exercised. Whether every module the shell needs from lib/ can be re-exported this way — some take locks, spawn processes, or hold module-level state — was not tested, and the answer may differ per module.

The adapter is a convention here, not a checked rule. Nothing in this probe stops a component importing `../../lib/planning.js` and bypassing the guard entirely. That is REQ-0021's territory and it is unbuilt.

notes: ⚠️ THE PLAIN-NODE CHECK IS THE POINT OF THIS PROBE. `server-only` resolves `react-server` to `empty.js` only inside the RSC compiler; everywhere else it resolves to `index.js`, which THROWS. Measured directly: importing it under bare Node throws "This module cannot be imported from a Client Component module." So the obvious placement — mark `lib/` and be done — would break every CLI in `bin/` and the entire test suite, which import `lib/` under plain Node.
